binders: An arbitrary natural number n, implicitly universally quantified and allowed to be zero.
Real n-by-n matrices A, Atilde, truncError, and roundingError.
Real scalars epsilon, beta, and gammaC.
hypotheses: Atilde = A + truncError exactly; equivalently, Atilde(i,j) = A(i,j) + truncError(i,j) for all i,j in Fin n.
computed = (Atilde + roundingError)v exactly; equivalently, computed(i) = sum over j in Fin n of (Atilde(i,j) + roundingError(i,j))*v(j) for every i.
||truncError||_F <= epsilon*beta, where ||.||_F denotes the matrix norm selected by D003.
conclusions: There exists a real n-by-n matrix totalError.
For that same totalError, computed = (A + totalError)v exactly; coordinatewise, computed(i) = sum over j in Fin n of (A(i,j) + totalError(i,j))*v(j).
For that same totalError, ||totalError||_F <= gammaC*||A||_F + epsilon*(1 + gammaC)*beta.
mathematical_definitions: Fin n is the index set {0,...,n-1}; when n=0 it is empty.
Matrix-vector multiplication is (Mx)(i) = sum over all j in Fin n of M(i,j)x(j).
The notation ||M||_F here denotes exactly Matrix.frobeniusNormedRing.norm M, the norm selected in D003.
A direct witness justified by the hypotheses is totalError = truncError + roundingError, although the conclusion itself does not require the existential witness to equal this matrix.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite dimension n, real square matrices A, Atilde, truncError, and roundingError, real vectors v and computed, and nonnegative real parameters epsilon, beta, and gammaC, suppose Atilde is exactly A plus truncError, computed is exactly the product of Atilde plus roundingError with v, the norm of truncError is at most epsilon*beta, and the norm of roundingError is at most gammaC times the norm of Atilde. Then there is a real square matrix totalError such that computed is exactly (A + totalError)v and the norm of totalError is at most gammaC*||A||_F + epsilon*(1 + gammaC)*beta.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension n may be zero. Then Fin n is empty, the matrix and vector types are degenerate, the matrix-vector sums are empty, and the assertion becomes correspondingly trivial.
The statement is an implication, so it is vacuously true whenever any exact equality, nonnegativity condition, or norm bound in the antecedent fails.

If epsilon*beta = 0, the truncation bound forces truncError to have zero norm; if gammaC = 0, the rounding bound forces roundingError to have zero norm. Data incompatible with those consequences make the antecedent false.
The conclusion constrains totalError only through its norm and its action on the single fixed vector v. It does not assert the matrix identity A + totalError = Atilde + roundingError.
In particular, when v is the zero vector, the computed-vector equality places no additional constraint on totalError beyond consistency of the hypotheses and the norm bound.
The existential witness is not asserted to be unique and is not explicitly required to equal truncError + roundingError.
No norm or nonzero condition is imposed on v, and no forward-error bound comparing computed with Av is stated.
No invertibility, conditioning, rank, symmetry, or other structural assumption on A is encoded.
The error bounds are normwise matrix bounds, not componentwise bounds, and beta is merely an arbitrary nonnegative real parameter with no encoded relationship to A or v.
All arithmetic and equalities are over exact real numbers; no floating-point format, rounding mode, machine arithmetic semantics, or probabilistic error model is encoded.
ambiguities: The packet identifies the selected norm through Matrix.frobeniusNormedRing, but its body delegates the actual norm to Matrix.frobeniusSeminormedAddCommGroup without supplying that declaration's body. Therefore the exact entrywise closed formula, such as the standard square-root-of-sum-of-squares formula suggested by the identifier, cannot be derived solely from the supplied bodies.
